surface: Client logout and password change without JWT revocation
boundary: Stolen or leftover Bearer versus server session end
reason: create_access_token is stateless HS256 with default 43200 minute TTL and no jti denylist. Dashboard logout only removes localStorage token; mobile signOut only deletes SecureStore keys. PATCH /auth/password does not appear to rotate outstanding access tokens. This is session invalidation, not ordinary CSRF or credentialed CORS.

boundary: Device backup or other OS profile versus staff password
reason: AuthContext writes email and password under ct_mobile_login_credentials with AFTER_FIRST_UNLOCK and no requireAuthentication. Selected companions were custom-scheme and file-open only; backup, work-profile, and Android allowBackup behavior need a dedicated credential-store unit.

surface: GitHub push to Railway rebuild with no in-repo workflow
boundary: Untrusted branch or fork commit versus production Dockerfile/Procfile deploy identity
attack_class: SUPPLY-CHAIN-AND-RELEASE.md#Untrusted code in a privileged workflow
reason: Selected supply blocks were mutable inputs and build-context only. Railway auto-deploy from GitHub, branch protection, and who can push to the connected branch are a separate privileged-workflow unit. No .github workflows exist to compare.

surface: R2 bucket public development URL and CORS AllowedOrigins
boundary: Anonymous CDN or signed-URL caller versus catalog object bytes
reason: Selected cloud blocks were reachability and workload identity. Bucket ACL, public development URL, and presign expiry/key binding need their own unit; live R2 policy is not in source.

boundary: Catalogger versus Page connection metadata and post history
reason: Those GETs are authenticated and account-scoped but skip require_facebook_poster. They do not return tokens; they need a separate read-leak unit if catalogger visibility of page name and captions is in scope.

boundary: Catalogger JWT versus owner-documented R2 ops on the shared bucket
reason: UI-less leftover R2 ops: dashboard never calls these routes. DEPLOY.md says migrate-catalog is owner-only, but migrate_catalog_to_r2, r2_ping, and r2_cors_get only use get_current_user. Clients are blocked by enforce_client_http; cataloggers are not. Sibling POST /integrations/r2/cors does require is_owner. ping() writes and deletes _health/r2-ping.txt on the shared bucket. Distinct from the assigned legacy CLI unit and from hunter-cloud Railway/env reachability.
